title: Machine for querying comparison flags
statement: Let $l,N,W,U$ be natural numbers, let $p,n\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, let $r_s(i)$ be a family of bit words indexed by times $s$ and coordinates $i$, let $y_0,y_1$ be target bit words, and let $v$ be a bit-word tail. Suppose $|r_s(i)|\le W$ for every $s<N$ and every $i$, $|y_j|\le W$ for each $j\in\{0,1\}$, and each of the $l+5$ query words formed from the targets, the stream of packed rows followed by $v$, and the unary clock of length $N$ has length at most $U$. There exist a finite binary Turing machine $Q$ and natural numbers $c,e$ such that, on the packed query argument, $Q$ outputs in at most $2(2|a|+9+(l+5)(3U+7)+N(l(5W+7)+2W+7))+c(N+1)^e+2$ steps the optional-time code of the greatest $s<N$ for which the value of $r_s(p)$ plus the value of $y_1$ equals the value of $y_0$ plus the value of $r_s(n)$; if no such $s$ exists, it outputs the code for absence. Here $a$ denotes that packed argument and each word is interpreted as a little-endian binary numeral.
hypotheses_covered: $p,n$ are coordinates in a set of size $l$ and are distinct
$r_s(i)$ is a family of bit words
all row words with $s<N$ have length at most $W$
both target words have length at most $W$
all query words have length at most $U$
replaced: For distinct positive and negative coordinates, there exist a single machine $Q$ and constants $c, e$ such that on every canonical query argument, a packed row family, target words, and strict-prefix clock, $Q$ computes the optional-time code of the last row whose cross-sums match the targets, within twice the query ledger plus $c(N+1)^e + 2$ steps. Only canonical inputs are promised; callers must establish them.
